title: 5 Best Calendly Alternatives for 2026 - Akiflow
summary: Compare the best Calendly alternatives for 2026, including Akiflow, Cal.com, SavvyCal, Doodle and Google Calendar, with honest prices and tradeoffs.
body_markdown:
**Summary**


-


Akiflow is the best Calendly alternative for independent professionals who want availability, planning, meeting capture, and follow-up in one workflow.


-


Cal.com is the closer direct replacement for advanced team routing; SavvyCal, Doodle, and Google Calendar each serve a narrower scheduling job.


-


Compare the full meeting lifecycle, not only the booking page: conflict checks, routing, reminders, meeting capture, and action-item handoff all matter.


## What are the best Calendly alternatives in 2026?


The best Calendly alternatives in 2026 are Akiflow, Cal.com, SavvyCal, Doodle, and Google Calendar. Akiflow is our overall choice for an independent professional who wants booking, task planning, meeting capture, and follow-up in one product. Cal.com is the stronger direct alternative when advanced team routing is the main requirement.


Calendly remains the comparison baseline. Its Free plan includes one event type and one calendar. Standard costs $10 per seat per month billed yearly and adds unlimited event types, multiple calendars, payments, Zapier, webhooks, reminders, and outreach automation. Teams costs $16 per seat per month billed yearly and adds Salesforce, round robin, lead qualification, routing, and advanced administration.


This article reviews current official product, help, and pricing information as of August 24, 2026; it does not claim hands-on testing. We compared conflict checking, event types, routing, group coordination, reminders, booking limits, payments, meeting capture, task handoff, and documented plan prices. Those criteria expose why a cheaper booking page may still be the wrong operational choice.


Start with the reason for leaving Calendly. Pick Cal.com for team routing and APIs, SavvyCal for branded links and scheduling overlays, Doodle for group polling, or Google Calendar for a booking page inside an existing Google setup. Pick Akiflow when the meeting must remain connected to the tasks before and after it. The[calendar management guide](https://akiflow.com/blog/calendar-management-software-what-to-look-for) covers the broader system.


### Calendly alternatives compared


1.


**Akiflow**


-


**Best for:** Independent professionals planning follow-up


-


**Scheduling model:** Availability, meetings, tasks, and calendar


-


**Price:** $34 monthly or $19/mo billed yearly


-


**Main boundary:** Less specialized for organization routing


2.


**Cal.com**


-


**Best for:** Teams with routing requirements


-


**Scheduling model:** Event types, round robin, routing forms, and APIs


-


**Price:** Free individual; Teams $12/user/mo billed yearly


-


**Main boundary:** Advanced organization controls cost more


3.


**SavvyCal**


-


**Best for:** Branded individual and team scheduling


-


**Scheduling model:** Links, overlays, polls, and workflows


-


**Price:** Free polls; Basic $12/user/mo


-


**Main boundary:** Custom domains and no branding require Premium


4.


**Doodle**


-


**Best for:** Finding a time for a group


-


**Scheduling model:** Group polls plus booking pages


-


**Price:** Free; Pro $15/mo or $132/year in US


-


**Main boundary:** Not designed for advanced lead routing


5.


**Google Calendar**


-


**Best for:** Simple booking inside Google Calendar


-


**Scheduling model:** Appointment schedules and conflict blocking


-


**Price:** One booking page on personal accounts


-


**Main boundary:** Advanced options need an eligible subscription


## 1. Akiflow


Choose Akiflow if you are an independent professional who wants availability sharing to live inside the same task and calendar system used to plan the rest of the day. It is not merely a booking-link replacement: the product connects available time, meetings, task intake, calendar planning, and documented follow-up tools in one workflow.


Availability links can be manual or recurring, with single-use slots, locked calendars for conflict checking, meeting location and calendar selection, custom title and color, buffers, minimum notice, a daily meeting maximum, date ranges, and guest reminders. That covers the core booking job while keeping the resulting event on the calendar used for[task and calendar planning](https://akiflow.com/blog/best-apps-that-combine-calendar-to-do-list-2026) .


Akiflow's Meeting Assistant can join Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings, record and transcribe them, create summaries, extract action items into the Inbox, and draft follow-up emails. The official help page states a fair-use limit of 1,800 minutes per month, three hours per meeting, and 30-day recording retention. The dedicated[Meeting Assistant page](https://akiflow.com/meeting-assistant) explains the product workflow.


Pricing for Akiflow Pro is $34 on a monthly plan or an effective $19 per month with yearly billing, and a 7-day trial is available. The tradeoff is specialization: Cal.com documents deeper organization routing, sub-teams, SSO, SCIM, and related controls on higher tiers. Choose Akiflow when meetings are part of personal execution; choose a routing platform when booking administration is the primary system being purchased.


## 2. Cal.com


Choose Cal.com if the goal is a direct Calendly replacement with generous individual scheduling and stronger team-routing options. The Individual plan is free and includes unlimited event types and calendars, notifications, more than 100 integrations, payments, CRM sync, mobile and browser apps, and a Calendly import path.


Teams costs $12 per user per month billed yearly. It adds shared availability, round robin, managed and collective events, recurring events, routing forms, analytics, custom APIs, and branding controls. Organizations costs $28 per user per month billed yearly and adds sub-teams, advanced routing, SSO, SCIM, compliance, and permissions.


Those plan boundaries make Cal.com the best option here for a team that wants the scheduler itself to own routing logic. The current[Cal.com pricing page](https://cal.com/pricing) also makes it easy to compare with Calendly's $16 Teams rate, but price alone is incomplete: confirm which CRM, routing, administrative, and compliance features the organization actually needs.


The tradeoff is that Cal.com remains a scheduling platform. Its documented strengths do not replace the broader personal task-planning workflow in Akiflow. A team with advanced inbound routing should prefer Cal.com; a consultant who wants to plan the preparation and follow-up around each booked call may get more value from combining those steps in one execution system.


## 3. SavvyCal


Choose SavvyCal if polished scheduling links, calendar overlays, and team booking features matter more than enterprise routing depth. Its Free plan supports meeting polls, unlimited calendar connections, calendar overlays, and draft scheduling links. That creates a useful no-cost evaluation path without treating the free tier as a complete booking system.


Basic costs $12 per user per month and adds unlimited active links and teams, custom branding, collective and round-robin scheduling, conferencing and CRM integrations, Zapier, API access, analytics, and workflows. Premium costs $20 per user per month and adds custom domains, removed branding, Stripe, delegated access, and advanced analytics.


The plan design makes SavvyCal a strong fit for an individual or team that cares about the presentation of booking links and wants overlays or polls alongside conventional scheduling. Review the current[SavvyCal pricing page](https://savvycal.com/pricing) to decide whether Basic contains enough branding and automation or Premium is required.


The tradeoff is tier placement. Custom domains, removed SavvyCal branding, Stripe, and delegated access sit in Premium. Cal.com provides a different path for organizational routing and permissions, while Doodle is simpler for finding consensus in a group. Choose SavvyCal for its scheduling-link workflow rather than assuming every meeting tool solves the same coordination problem.


## 4. Doodle


Choose Doodle if the central problem is finding a time that works for a group. The Free plan can create group meetings, a booking page, and sign-up sheets. Its defining advantage in this comparison is the poll: participants can respond to proposed options without requiring the organizer to build advanced routing rules.


Doodle Pro costs $15 monthly or $132 yearly in the United States and adds calendar sync, tracking, branding, an ad-free experience, reminders, booking pages, and one-to-one scheduling. Team costs $21 per user monthly or $16 per user monthly billed yearly and adds centralized administration and shared team features.


The official[Doodle pricing help page](https://help.doodle.com/en/articles/9457366-how-much-does-doodle-cost) clearly separates group coordination from the paid scheduling and administration layers. That makes Doodle easy to place: use it when participant input is the hard part; use a routing platform when leads or customers must be qualified and assigned automatically.


Doodle is narrower than the other choices for a reason. A group poll is often the fastest way to coordinate a committee, class, or multi-company meeting, but it is not a substitute for Cal.com's routing forms or Akiflow's task follow-up. The best tool depends on whether the meeting begins with consensus, a booking rule, or an execution workflow.


## 5. Google Calendar


Choose Google Calendar if one booking page and native calendar conflict checking cover the requirement. Appointment schedules provide adjustable availability, a shared link or embed, automatic conflict blocking, recurring schedules, buffers, daily booking limits, co-hosts, reminders, and payments on eligible plans. The main benefit is remaining inside a calendar many people already use.


Personal accounts can create one booking page. More advanced booking-page features require an eligible Google Workspace or Google One subscription, so the apparently simple option still needs a plan check. The exact eligibility rules matter more than a generic free-versus-paid label because several capabilities depend on the account type.


Google Calendar is a credible Calendly replacement for straightforward individual scheduling, but it is not the default choice for every team. Cal.com documents deeper routing and administration, Doodle handles polling, and Akiflow connects booking to personal task execution. Choose Google when the booking requirement is modest and the surrounding workflow already belongs in the Google ecosystem.


**Tip** Run one real booking from shared link to follow-up task. Record every manual handoff; that reveals whether the scheduler supports the full meeting workflow or only the booking step.


## Which Calendly alternative should you choose?


Choose Akiflow when a booked meeting must remain connected to task planning, calendar execution, notes, and follow-up. Choose Cal.com when routing and team administration define the project. Choose SavvyCal for branded scheduling links, Doodle for group polling, and Google Calendar when a basic booking page inside the existing calendar is enough.


Test the complete meeting path, not only the public booking screen. Create a link, attempt a conflict, book from a second email address, inspect reminders, join the meeting, record a decision, and assign a follow-up task. Note every point where information must be copied into another system. That handoff cost often matters more than cosmetic differences between booking pages.


For teams, document routing before comparing plans. List the lead fields, assignment rules, calendars, CRM destination, ownership exceptions, and administrative controls required. Cal.com and Calendly place different capabilities in different tiers. A lower seat price is useful only if the chosen tier includes the actual routing model and the integrations needed to operate it.


Our overall recommendation is Akiflow for independent professionals because its documented workflow extends beyond availability into meeting capture and action-item execution. The deal-breaker is organizational routing: when sub-teams, advanced routing, SSO, SCIM, compliance, or centralized administration are mandatory, select the specialized scheduling platform whose paid tier explicitly includes them.


## Frequently asked questions


### Which Calendly alternative is best for independent professionals?


Akiflow is the best fit here for independent professionals who want scheduling tied to personal execution. It combines availability links, calendar planning, tasks, Meeting Assistant summaries, and action-item extraction into the Inbox. Cal.com is a better direct scheduling choice when routing depth matters more. Akiflow Pro costs $34 monthly or $19 per month billed yearly.


### Is Cal.com cheaper than Calendly for teams?


On annual billing, Cal.com Teams is listed at $12 per user per month and Calendly Teams at $16 per seat per month. Cal.com includes shared availability, round robin, managed and collective events, recurring events, routing forms, analytics, custom APIs, and branding controls. Compare required integrations and administration too; a lower rate does not establish equivalent scope by itself.


### When should I choose SavvyCal instead of Cal.com?


Choose SavvyCal when calendar overlays, branded links, polls, delegated access, or its specific Basic and Premium feature split matches the workflow. Choose Cal.com when the requirement centers on advanced routing, sub-teams, SSO, SCIM, compliance, or organization permissions. Both support team scheduling, so the deciding factor should be the exact paid-tier capability rather than a generic feature count.


### Is Doodle still useful for group scheduling?


Yes. Doodle's group poll remains a distinct solution when several participants need to express availability before a time is selected. Free supports group meetings, a booking page, and sign-up sheets. Pro adds calendar sync, tracking, branding, reminders, and one-to-one scheduling. Choose a routing product instead when meetings must be qualified or assigned automatically rather than decided by participant consensus.


### Can Google Calendar replace Calendly?


Google Calendar can replace Calendly for a straightforward booking workflow. Personal accounts can create one booking page, with availability controls and calendar conflict blocking. Advanced options depend on an eligible Google Workspace or Google One subscription. It becomes a weaker replacement when the organization needs multiple routing paths, specialized administration, or lead qualification beyond the documented appointment-schedule scope.
